audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart gives Ekko 6 of 7 stages and ends on 'Skill'; the packet and the content layer both give him 5 and hand the last two to Aurelion Sol. The two layers rendered different answers for 'First item' and '2+ items'.
audit.why: 48.98% over 541 games is a slight loss, which the Ekko x5 early chart already reflects. The last two rows belong to Aurelion Sol on range alone: Falling Star reaches 1250 against Chronobreak's 850, and Rod of Ages buys the HP to survive one Phase Dive rotation. The full layer's own whys for rows 5 and 6 already describe Aurelion Sol winning — only the side field disagreed.
audit.corrected: phases[5].side and phases[6].side both set to Aurelion Sol, matching win[5] and win[6]. Difficulty left at HARD 8/10 — the sub-50% win rate supports it.
sources: packet winRate 48.98 over 541 games and its levelChart

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and content late build Shadowflame/Stormsurge; the full layer's itemization builds Rod of Ages, Archangel's, Liandry's, Rabadon's. Separately, Chronobreak's rank scaling — the biggest spike in the matchup — was never stated.
audit.why: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1, 80s at rank 2 and 50s at rank 3. It more than doubles in availability across the game, which is the actual reason his aggression escalates; the page just said his all-ins are 'risk-free'.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text, late, breakdown.spikes, breakdown.feeding and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten around Rod of Ages and the 110/80/50 curve.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never on the page. Parallel Convergence is the ability that beats Aurelion Sol, not Chronobreak — the page made Chronobreak the focus and reduced Convergence to 'zone control'.
audit.why: enemyKit W: 'If Ekko enters the anomaly, he gains shielding and stuns enemies by suspending them in time.' Both Breath of Light and Astral Flight carry the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it'), so that stun ends the beam AND drops the flight. It is placed from 1600 range, well outside anything Aurelion Sol has. Four of the five missingInteractions entries (your-channel-punished, shield-absorbs-burst, untargetable-dodges-burst, needs-antiheal) were all absent.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, enemyWin, tradeBad, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d, spikes[0].text and content early now state the anomaly stun, the 1600 placement range, and the channel cancel. dosFull[1].d and ahead cover the untargetable window and Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Ekko's slow-and-stun combo out of Parallel Convergence is the core threat — once you're caught in that zone, the follow-up burst chains before Astral Flight can save you, so play with more space than usual around his zone placements. Farm the back line with Q from 750, let Timewinder hit minions, and never stand on ground he has already marked.

edits.before: Level 6 Chronobreak makes his all-ins essentially risk-free since a bad engage can be undone by the reset, so expect more aggression from him in this window than most other laners. Hold your escape tools defensively, avoid extended trades near his zone, and focus on surviving to your power spike rather than forcing fights.
edits.after: Chronobreak at 6 is 110 seconds, and it makes a failed dive survivable — he goes untargetable, rewinds, and heals a share of what you dealt. Expect him to take fights he should not. edits.before: Once your core item lands you out-range and out-damage his combo entirely — Voice of Light punishes his approach before Convergence ever gets set up, and your Q collision burst outpaces anything he can land in a single rotation. edits.after: Once Rod of Ages and Archangel's are done you out-range him — Falling Star stuns from 1250 before Chronobreak's 850 is even a choice, and permanent stardust makes Breath of Light burn through the Convergence shield. From here you pick the distance and he has to cross it into the black hole.

notes: Difficulty left at HARD 8/10 and tone at #ff5d6c here, unlike brand/cassiopeia/diana — the 48.98% win rate is the only one of my eight that actually supports a hard rating, so I did not touch it. The packet's suspectName on 'Use Chronobreak' is a false positive: Chronobreak is Ekko's real R name. The full and content charts disagreed on rows 5 and 6 before this edit (full read Ekko then Skill, content read Aurelion Sol twice); both now read Ekko x5 / Aurelion Sol / Aurelion Sol, matching the packet. The single most valuable correction on this page is that Parallel Convergence, not Chronobreak, is the ability that beats Aurelion Sol — the whole page was built around the wrong focus ability, and focus.text still reads 'Ekko Chronobreak'. I did not edit focus.text because I could not tell from the brief whether that field drives the loading-screen tracker UI or is purely cosmetic; see questionsForUser.
